beats.headline: Something for tier two
beats.text: Katia spends one of her coupons on a Training Room, which trains any skill that is not a magic spell for an hour a day, supposedly as if the crawler were really fighting with it. It costs 250,000 gold, and it will not train anything explosive. Mordecai says tier two will have something called a Bomber's Studio, which would let Carl practise blowing shit up. It joins the list of upgrades Carl still wants, beside the expensive kitchen ones that serve food with buffs and the kennel ones that do the same for Mongo.

beats.headline: A class with a room
beats.text: At the filthy screen where he picks his class specialty, Carl has three choices. Mordecai insists on the melee one. The Guerilla gets the Advanced Trap Maker's Workshop, which is only a table. The Agent Provocateur gets plus one intelligence a level, a skill level for his Sapper's table, plus two to Explosives Handling, faster explosives training and access to the advanced Bomb Maker's Workshop: an entire room, where he could precisely tune his explosives, and which a few recipes in his cookbook need. With a minute left and the coin slot's orange light blinking, he clicks the third choice. Sorry, Mordecai.

beats.headline: A private bowling alley
beats.text: Carl has bought the advanced bomber's studio alongside a magic workshop, which leaves them only 100K gold. The room is only about ten feet wide but long, like a private bowling alley. Nothing in its testing area really explodes: he can copy a design or a bomb, build a virtual village, set it off, pause it and see which way it blows, though the system sometimes gives only a range, and the cookbook stresses it is no guarantee. Being advanced, it can also test virtual bombs he does not have, though for now only with items in his inventory. At the very back is a level-one bench for examining and dissecting explosives. On it he sets Carl's Doomsday Scenario, out of his inventory for the first time since he grabbed it, copies it into the simulator and puts it back, his hands trembling.

beats.headline: Freshly upgraded, still waiting
beats.text: Before heading out into Old Havana, Carl wants to get into the craft room and play with his new automaton pieces, and his bomber's studio has just been upgraded, so he wants to go in there too. Mordecai is already making noises about the crafting table upgrade coupons. Carl tells him they should get their bearings first, and goes back to ring the exit stairwell with traps instead.

beats.headline: Part of Rosetta's price
beats.text: Rosetta wants the toraline and what is left of the ink Shi Maria brewed for Carl's tattoo. Then she wants access to his saferoom, so they can get to work. Give me access to your bomber's studio, too, she says. And three million gold. She glares at the finger-sized sliver of vegetable he hands over. Better make it four million.

beats.headline: Justice Light needs nothing
beats.text: Losing the saferoom entrance will put base a half-hour ride away by tracked vehicle, and more. Justice Light will lose access to Carl's sapper's table and the bomber's studio, and Rosetta easy access to the alchemy table and Mordecai. The one-winged skyfowl, sewing a folded piece of red paper to an orange one in the corner, tilts his head and stretches out his lone wing. It's okay, the eagle says. I already have everything I need.

beats.headline: Left on Donut's side
beats.text: Before Carl leaves the Royal Court of Princess Donut, the garage will not be affected by his leaving, and Imani is ready to join his segregated room back into the guild. Most of his crafting tables, the bomber's studio included, will remain on Donut's side. It will make things easier once he rejoins. Plus, if he dies, she will not lose it all. He clicks Yes.
